name: Autonomous Chromatophore Tattoo
description: A hybrid of geneprint and chromatophore technology that produces small, localized patches of dynamic pigment cells that animate in response to physiological signals — heartbeat, breathing, stress hormones, or voluntary control. The most popular configuration is a design that pulses with the user's heartbeat, creating a living rhythm visible on the skin. Other configurations include stress-reactive designs that shift color during emotional arousal, breath-synced patterns on the torso, and manually animated designs controlled by subdermal nerve signals. The patches are small — typically covering an area the size of a palm — and multiple patches can be placed to create coordinated full-body animations. In GLMZ's club scene, coordinated pulse tattoos that sync across multiple people on the same dance floor are a major art form.
source_organism: Sepia officinalis (common cuttlefish), synthetic neural-pigment interface
manufacturer: Lacuna Genomics (premium animated), various clinics (basic pulse)
procedure: Localized dermal injection, single session per patch
side_effects: Patches broadcast physiological data — your heartbeat is visible to anyone watching
Animation glitches during illness or drug use
Multiple patches may desynchronize, creating discordant visual effects
Rare: patches develop autonomous animation patterns not linked to any physiological signal
social_perception: Trendy and expressive. Pulse tattoos are a social currency — the quality and complexity of your animations signals your taste and tier. Coordinated group animations are a performance art form.
story_hooks: A dancer's pulse tattoo begins broadcasting a heartbeat that isn't theirs — someone has hacked the chromatophore link to display a dead person's recorded cardiac rhythm as a message
A pulse tattoo's autonomous animation develops into a recognizable pattern — it's writing text, one letter at a time, and the message is a warning
